result:
`build_invoice` now looks up each tax rate once per country instead of once per line. I haven't timed it, because I don't have Northwind's October data. Most of the 50 seconds was spent re-reading the tax JSON files for every line, so this should cut it a lot.

All test files pass when run individually. A full `pytest` run hung once in my environment and I didn't get a clean full-suite result. I never found out why it hung.

**What changed**
- The rate lookup in `workspace/meterbill/meterbill/invoices/builder.py` now uses a dict local to the call, keyed by country. Within one invoice the tenant and issue date never change, so the country is the only thing that affects the rate.
- The dict is discarded when `build_invoice` returns. Nothing is shared between invoice runs, and the tax resolver and store are untouched, so they still read the files on every lookup.
- A tenant's override file edit or a revoked exemption is picked up on the next invoice, which keeps the rule from the stale-exemption incident. Rates, rounding and errors are unchanged.
- A new test in `tests/test_invoices.py` checks two things: each country is looked up once per build, and nothing is remembered between builds.

I also updated `CLAUDE.md`. I moved the tax-cache item from "Next" into the decision, bumped the test count to 378, and added a note. If runs are still slow, profile rating and event reading before widening the cache.
